column1: What is a request?
column28:
Requests are like emails from your customers asking for help. Like email, you can respond to the reporter and add attachments. Unlike email, you can set all kinds of useful information, such as labels, priority and a status showing where the request is up to.

h3. Try it out

When you've finished exploring this request, *update the status* to resolve it and let the reporter know it's done.

column1: Capturing customer email requests
column28:
The easiest way for your customer's to request help is by sending an email to your service space. When emails get sent to your space, they land in your queue as a request (just like this one).

h3. Try it out

Email a request to *Demo service space's* support email address ( [mailto:redacted@example.invalid] ) to see how it looks for your customers and agents.
column90: 22/Nov/26 4:20 PM;redacted-account-id;But wait, the conversation is only just getting started. For your customers, getting in touch is as easy as responding to the notification they receive in their email inbox.

column1: Agents & customers
column28:
*Agents* are the members of your team that answer and resolve requests from your *Customers*. In Jira Service Management, you only pay for agents and not the customers who raise requests. In other words, you can support as many customers as you need without paying any extra.

Ready to invite your team? Look for *Invite team* on your space's sidebar (you may need to select *Back to space* to get out of your queues menu) to invite your team as agents.

column1: Collecting custom request details
column28:
Define and organize incoming requests using *request types*. Capture and track relevant details upfront by customizing the *request types* you want to show up on the help center. You can also add *internal fields* to track details that you don't want your customers to see.

h3. Try it out

We've given you some request types to try. Visit *Channels* (you may need to click *Back to space* to get out of your queues menu) to raise a request via your service space's Help Center and see them in action.

column1: Triaging requests into queues
column28:
Organise your customer's requests into queues to help your team stay focused while you keep track of what needs to be done. Build your own *queues* to split requests by agents, request types, office locations, status or your team's custom fields.
h3. Try it out
Build a queue to show your recently resolved requests. Select *New queue* and update the status filter to only show requests set to *Resolved*.
